module_title: Intermediate Grid - Ashokan Inscriptions, Scripts, and Foreign Ambassadors
introduction: Ashoka was the first Indian king to speak directly to his people through his inscriptions. This intermediate tier focuses on the classification of Ashokan edicts, the historic decipherment of his script, and the sequence of Greek ambassadors in the Mauryan court.

core_concepts.title: Decipherment of Ashokan Edicts
core_concepts.description: Ashoka's edicts remained a mystery for centuries. They were finally deciphered in **1837** by **James Prinsep**, a British antiquary and colonial administrator. Most inscriptions refer to Ashoka as 'Devanampiya Piyadasi' (Beloved of the Gods).

core_concepts.title: Crucial Major Rock Edicts (MRE)
core_concepts.description:
- **MRE XIII (13th):** The longest and most important edict. It vividly describes the **Kalinga War**, Ashoka's remorse, and his policy of Dhamma.
- **MRE I:** Prohibits animal sacrifice and festive gatherings.
- **Bhabru Inscription:** The only inscription where Ashoka explicitly expresses his faith in the Buddhist Trinity (Buddha, Dhamma, Sangha).

core_concepts.title: Scripts Used in Ashokan Inscriptions
core_concepts.description:
Ashoka used four different scripts based on the geography of his empire:
- **Brahmi:** Used in the majority of the empire (Eastern, Central, and Southern India).
- **Kharoshthi:** Used in the North-Western region (modern-day Pakistan).
- **Aramaic and Greek:** Used in the extreme North-West (modern-day Afghanistan).

core_concepts.title: Foreign Ambassadors to the Mauryan Court
core_concepts.description:
- **Megasthenes:** Sent by Seleucus Nicator to Chandragupta Maurya.
- **Deimachus:** Sent by Antiochus I (Syrian King) to Bindusara's court.
- **Dionysius:** Sent by Ptolemy II Philadelphus (Egyptian King) to Bindusara/Ashoka's court.

important_entities.name: Maski and Gujarra Edicts
important_entities.significance: For a long time, historians only knew of a king named 'Devanampiya Piyadasi'. It was the minor rock edicts found at **Maski** (Karnataka) and **Gujarra** (Madhya Pradesh) that explicitly used the name 'Ashoka', proving that Piyadasi and Ashoka were the same person.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation:
Examiners often confuse students by mixing language and script. 
- The **Language** of most Ashokan edicts was **Prakrit** (the language of the common masses).
- The **Script** (how it was written) was predominantly **Brahmi**. Do not select Sanskrit for Ashokan edicts.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: The number 13 is traditionally considered unlucky in Western culture. The Kalinga war was highly 'unlucky' (disastrous) for the people of Kalinga. Hence, Kalinga War = 13th Rock Edict.

exam_strategy_tips: In UPSC Prelims and CDS, James Prinsep's name (1837 decipherment) and the 13th Major Rock Edict are exceptionally high-frequency topics. You must also know that Ashoka used Kharoshthi script (written right to left) in the North-West.
